title: Non-split sharply 2- and 3-transitive groups in SL_n(\mathbb Z)
summary: We prove that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ contains a non-split sharply 2-transitive subgroup, answering a question of Glasner and Gulko. We also prove that $\mathrm{SL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ contains a non-split sharply 3-transitive subgroup, but that $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ does not contain an infinite sharply 3-transitive subgroup.
